units.translation: The prepositions εἰς and ἐν, to which in Latin one word in corresponds, differ among the Greeks in that εἰς (like in with the accusative) signifies motion into a place, and ἐν (like in with the ablative) rest in a place, and indeed both often in such a way that not the place itself that is named, but the vicinity of the place is understood.

as he said ἰδέσθαι εἰς [to look upon] Suppl. 103 ἰδέσθω δ᾽ εἰς ὕβριν [let him look upon the outrage]. [But Ch. 232 ἰδοῦ — εἰς δὲ θήρειον γραφήν [behold — and into the beastly writing], εἰς δὲ is corrupted from ἠδὲ, which Turnebus restored.]
Frequent is ἐς τὸ πᾶν [to the whole], i.e. πάντως or παντελῶς, utterly, altogether, for examples see under πᾶς.
